meta.title: Battle for La Roma — A real-time strategy game for Mexico City
meta.description: A free classic RTS set in a satirical Mexico City. Gather, build, climb four ages and take La Roma. Play in your browser or on macOS.
meta.ogAlt: Four factions fight over the Cibeles roundabout in Battle for La Roma

suggest.text: Esta página también está en español.

hero.title: From rooftop room to rooftop bar, reservations only.
hero.lede: A classic real-time strategy game set in a satirical Mexico City. Gather resources, build your base, raise your crew and climb four ages until La Roma is yours. The rent goes up on its own. You'll have to earn it.
hero.facts: Free · Browser and macOS · Campaign, skirmish and private online rooms
hero.artAlt: Concept art: four factions fight over the Cibeles roundabout in Roma Norte

items: Breaking: rich kid asks for valet parking for his tank
Specialty café now charges you to smell the coffee
Office drone requests to work from home mid-battle

play.title:
This is not a brunch.
It's an RTS.
play.intro: Build, gather, recruit and conquer in real time, just like the classics you grew up on. Except here the map has potholes and a single roundabout is worth more than your apartment.

features.title: From empty lot to empire
features.body: Put up a command post, housing and barracks. Expand before somebody shows up with a mixed-use render and a “Coming soon” banner.

features.title: Money doesn't grow on jacarandas
features.body: Food, Materials, Varos (cash) and Land. Put your people to work and plan every trip: each run counts, like the bus at rush hour.

features.title: Whoever holds the center, rules
features.body: Train troops, scout the map and win by razing the rival command post or holding the center until the clock runs out. Nobody gets evicted on their own.

play.shotAlt: Gameplay capture: two armies clash next to the center of the La Roma map

resources.name: Food
resources.body: Tacos, markets and urban gardens. Nobody conquers anything hungry.

resources.name: Materials
resources.body: Bricks, rebar and whatever was left over from the build across the street.

resources.name: Varos
resources.body: Slang for cash. No varos, no troops; no troops, no neighborhood.

resources.name: Land
resources.body: The most contested resource in the city. Just ask any landlord.

ages.title:
Four ages.
One zip code
you can't afford.
ages.intro: You don't advance from Stone Age to Bronze Age here. You advance from out-of-towner with two suitcases to someone who says “terroir” without irony. Each age unlocks new buildings, technologies and troops. The character never changed. The neighborhood did.

cards.title:
Out-of-Towner
Age
cards.quote: “It's cozy, but it gets lots of natural light.”
cards.who: The landlord, about a rooftop room in Doctores.
cards.body: Two suitcases, a speaker with more miles on it than you and the unshakable belief that the metro is “super close.” You came to conquer the capital. First you need a water jug.
cards.alt: Gameplay capture in the first age: one command post and a few workers

cards.title:
University
Age
cards.quote: “It's a chill plan, I only brought three liters of jungle juice.”
cards.who: The guy who never brings anything chill.
cards.body: You've mastered changing metro lines, you debate the nation's future sitting on volcanic rock and you submit the essay at 11:59. The revolution starts tomorrow. Tonight there's a party.
cards.alt: Gameplay capture: the base grows with a depot, housing and a registry

cards.title:
Godín
Age
cards.quote: “Can we align on a quick call?”
cards.who: Your boss, from a meeting that could have been an email.
cards.body: A godín is an office drone, and now that's you. Backpack swapped for a badge, revolution for grocery vouchers. You've mastered Excel, basket tacos and looking busy on Teams.
cards.alt: Gameplay capture: troops take the Cibeles roundabout

cards.title:
Gentrification
Age
cards.quote: “It's a small-batch mezcal with notes of nostalgia.”
cards.who: You. You said that. Out loud.
cards.body: You wear linen, ask where the ice comes from and your coffee has a biography. Your lease comes with clauses in English. Congratulations: you're the problem now.
cards.alt: Gameplay capture: two large armies clash in the center of La Roma

ages.footnote: *Water, power, gas and dignity not included.
ages.epilogueTitle: From campus jungle juice to signature cocktails in Polanco.
ages.epilogueBody: Four ages of progress. None of them gets your rooftop-room deposit back.
ages.caption: The age images are real in-game captures.

factions.title:
Four factions.
Zero HOA
agreements.
factions.intro: They all arrived with a plan. None of them planned for traffic on Insurgentes. Each faction plays differently: pick one to see its strategy.

list.name: Regios
list.short: Aggressive investors: carry more, pay more.
list.quote: “What do you mean you don't take dollars?”
list.detail: From Monterrey, the industrial north. Their workers carry more per trip, so the economy takes off fast. In exchange, every fighter costs one extra Varo. The budget is in charge… and it shows.
list.alt: Concept portrait of the Regios faction
list.unitBody: A mirrey is a flashy rich kid. He arrives in an armored SUV and settles everything with the company card. Very expensive elite: his card swipe leaves enemies wondering what just happened.

list.name: Poblanos
list.short: Stubborn defense: buildings that won't fall.
list.quote: “The mole is not up for negotiation.”
list.detail: From Puebla. Their buildings take 20% more punishment. Their workers carry less, so plan your trips. Slow, but nobody moves them off their block.
list.alt: Concept portrait of the Poblanos faction
list.unitBody: Heals nearby allies and boosts Food production. No army fights well before breakfast.

list.name: Oaxaqueños
list.short: Fast economy: gather and build quicker.
list.quote: “Relax, this is already organized. For three generations now.”
list.detail: From Oaxaca. They gather faster and lend a hand with construction. Their buildings are lighter: a fast economy needs someone watching its back.
list.alt: Concept portrait of the Oaxaqueños faction
list.unitBody: Long-range siege shaped like an alebrije, a brightly painted folk-art creature. Heavy craftsmanship, quite literally.

list.name: Veracruzanos
list.short: Speed and trade: always first to arrive.
list.quote: “Turn it up, they can't hear it all the way to Cibeles!”
list.detail: From the Gulf coast. They move faster and squeeze more out of trade, ideal for opening routes. Their buildings are light, so don't leave the base alone while you're out claiming streets.
list.alt: Concept portrait of the Veracruzanos faction
list.unitBody: An amphibious unit for canal maps, built from Xochimilco's flower boats. It arrives by water, colorful awning and all.

factions.note: Fictional factions with game strategies, not portraits of real people. No Regio was harmed in the making of this page (okay, maybe one, but he already asked for a refund).
factions.unitAltPrefix: Concept art of the unique unit

modes.title:
Five ways
to start a fight.
modes.intro: All of this ships in the free browser and macOS builds. No invite, no waitlist, no cover charge.

list.title: You vs. the AI
list.body: Five maps and three difficulty levels, from an AI that's still learning to one that reads your every move.

list.title: Three chapters
list.body: From Copilco to Narvarte, then on to the battle for La Roma. Your progress saves on your device.

list.title: A monumental build
list.body: Build it in the Godín Age and defend it for 90 seconds. Like any construction project in Mexico City, the hard part is not getting shut down.

list.title: With an AI ally
list.body: You and an AI with its own economy against two more. Like a group project, except your partner actually pulls their weight.

list.title: Online with a friend
list.body: Create a room, share the code and play whoever you like. Any friendship that survives is the real thing.

city.eyebrow: 05 · Welcome to the city where everything is 40 minutes away
city.title:
Mexico City is the
battlefield.
city.intro: Streets, neighborhoods and roundabouts you'll recognize, or at least remember from somebody's travel reel.

playable.name: La Roma · three sizes
playable.body: The Cibeles roundabout, contested since before the first specialty café opened.

playable.name: Narvarte
playable.body: Neat grid blocks, wide avenues and nobody who knows where to park.

playable.name: Copilco
playable.body: Next door to the main campus. The campaign starts here (so does the insomnia).

city.visionTitle: Coming soon (or so says the render)

vision.name: Historic Center
vision.body: Marble, domes and four centuries of protest marches. Even the pigeons have a backstory.

vision.name: Ciudad Universitaria
vision.body: The main campus. The research never ends. Neither does the semester.

vision.name: Chapultepec
vision.body: A castle on a hill: the high ground every general (and every influencer) wants.

vision.name: Coyoacán
vision.body: The revolution will be artisanal. Barter and unsolicited opinions accepted.

vision.name: Xochimilco
vision.body: Battles on flower boats. Mariachis count as reinforcements.

vision.name: Santa Fe
vision.body: Corporate reinforcements. Estimated arrival: after rush hour.

faq.eyebrow: 06 · Questions your aunt would ask in the family group chat
faq.title: Before it kicks off.

items.q: Is it a real strategy game?
items.a: Yes. Economy, construction, four ages, combat and territory control, all in real time. If you love classic RTS games, you'll feel right at home (no co-signer required).
Nothing. It's free in your browser and on macOS. The only fees are the building maintenance dues, and those aren't ours.

items.q: Do I need to know Mexico City to get it?
items.a: No. The rules and objectives explain themselves; the references are a bonus. Miss a joke and you can still win the match.

items.q: What language is the game in?
items.a: Spanish and English, both this site and the game. It starts in your browser or computer's language, and you can switch anytime under Settings → Language.

items.q: How do I play online with someone?
items.a: From the menu, create a private room and share the code with whoever you want to challenge. It's one on one, and you don't need anyone's invitation.

items.q: Does it work on Windows or my phone?
items.a: The browser version runs on Windows, Linux and Mac computers, and there's also a macOS download. It has touch controls, but we can't vouch for phones yet: a bigger screen is better.
Yes, on your device, with no accounts or cloud. Clear your browser data and your progress goes with it; to move a match elsewhere, export it from Settings.

items.q: Is the Cibeles roundabout really in it?
items.a: Yes: it's the heart of the La Roma map and the spot everyone wants to control. Of course the fight happens there.

footer.tagline: Made with love for Mexico City and a reasonable suspicion of cafés that describe their water.
footer.disclaimer: An independent work of fiction and satire. The neighborhoods, institutions and cultures shown inspire an imaginary world; the jokes target situations and habits, never anyone's dignity. The cover, factions, unique units, city and landmarks are concept art; the ages and gameplay section show real in-game captures.
